message: The Titanic data has a binary target (Survived) and mixed numeric/categorical features. High‑cardinality free‑text columns (Name, Ticket, Cabin) need signal extraction before being dropped to avoid over‑fitting. The profile shows strong skew in Fare (skew=4.79) and missing values in Age (19.9%) and Cabin (77%). Tree‑based models can handle missing values, but we still add missing indicators (default true). We extract: • Title from Name (regex ", (\\w+)\.") – titles are known strong predictors. • Ticket prefix from Ticket (regex "^([A-Za-z./]+)") – groups tickets by issuing agency. • Cabin deck from Cabin (regex "^([A-Za-z])") – deck correlates with location on the ship. After extraction we drop the raw high‑cardinality columns (Name, Ticket, Cabin) and the identifier (PassengerId). Family size (SibSp + Parch + 1) is created via a group‑size feature on ["SibSp","Parch"]. We also add a text‑length feature for Name, which captures name length information. Fare is heavily right‑skewed, so we log‑transform it. Frequency‑encode the newly created categorical features (TicketPrefix, CabinDeck) to give tree models a numeric representation without exploding cardinality. No datetime columns exist, and no ratio features are needed beyond the family‑size derived column. The target is binary, so we do not log‑transform it.

We include two LightGBM variants to explore the trade‑off between more trees with a very low learning rate and a more regularised shallow tree setup. A HistGradientBoosting model adds a different boosting implementation with its own regularisation knobs. Finally an ExtraTrees model provides a diverse bagging‑based ensemble. With 4 experiments we set ensemble_top_k=2 so the greedy ensemble will consider the best 4 models.
